problems.quote: An axolotl that has eaten guards a box 32 blocks wide and 16 blocks high around its bowl for the next five minutes
problems.issue: guard_radius (32) and guard_radius_y (16) are radii, not box dimensions. findTarget uses `new AABB(bowlPos).inflate(radius, radiusY, radius)` and isWithinGuardZone compares |x - bowl| <= radius, so the box reaches 32 blocks in EVERY horizontal direction and 16 up and down — roughly 65 x 33 x 65 blocks. The page states it correctly further down ('inflated by guard_radius (32) horizontally and guard_radius_y (16) vertically'), so the two passages contradict each other.
problems.correction: "...guards a box that reaches 32 blocks in every horizontal direction and 16 blocks up and down from its bowl (about 65 blocks across, 33 high) for the next five minutes"

problems.quote: Vanilla keeps only the variant and the age and discards the rest of the entity, which would quietly destroy owner, bowl, experience, loot and worn armor.
problems.issue: Axolotl.saveToBucketTag (1.21.1, decompiled) writes Variant, Age AND the HAS_HUNTING_COOLDOWN expiry, and first calls Bucketable.saveDefaultDataToBucketTag, which stores CUSTOM_NAME, Health and the NoAI/Silent/NoGravity/Glowing/Invulnerable flags. What vanilla loses is the module's own state (data attachments), not 'the rest of the entity'.
problems.correction: "Vanilla carries only its own handful of fields — variant, age, hunting cooldown, health, name and a few flags — and drops everything else the entity held, which would quietly destroy owner, bowl, experience, loot and worn armor."

problems.quote: Priority runs from the top down; the first state that matches ends the pass.
problems.issue: Only Playing dead, Fleeing and Fed actually `return` from tickAxolotl. The Returning branch does not: after it re-asserts the way home it falls through to enforceTargetZone, tickStuckDetection and the Fed branch (which calls maybeAcquireTarget and can clear RETURNING in the same pass). That fall-through is precisely what makes returning interruptible, as the page itself explains two paragraphs later.
problems.correction: "Priority runs from the top down. Playing dead, Fleeing and Fed end the pass; Returning is handled and then falls through into the target scan below — which is what makes it interruptible."

problems.quote: Guardians never fight on land | Targets must be in water, and so must the axolotl.
problems.issue: The in-water requirement on the axolotl itself only gates NEW targets (maybeAcquireTarget's `!axolotl.isInWaterOrBubble() -> return`). The retaliation branch in onAxolotlHurt checks only `attacker.isInWaterOrBubble()`, and enforceTargetZone never drops a target because the axolotl left the water — a beached guardian keeps fighting until its air supply falls below 1200 (up to four minutes, per the page's own 'Dry land ends the shift').
problems.correction: "Targets must be in water; the axolotl must be in water to pick up a new target, and a beached one gives up only once its air runs low."

problems.quote: Drops from a mob a guardian killed are inserted straight into its five loot slots before they ever become item entities.
problems.issue: LivingDropsEvent hands the module a `Collection<ItemEntity>` (onLivingDrops iterates `event.getDrops()` and calls `iter.remove()`); the drops already exist as ItemEntity instances at that point — they are merely never added to the level.
problems.correction: "...inserted straight into its five loot slots before they are ever added to the world."

problems.quote: The module credits the owner on every hit a guardian lands (`victim.setLastHurtByPlayer(owner)`)
problems.issue: The actual call in onMobDamagedByAxolotl is `victim.setLastHurtByPlayer(ownerPlayer)`; `owner` is the UUID in that method, so the quoted line would not compile. Everything else about the mechanism is right.
